title: Every Loan Has a Home
request: Match each loan slip to its branch, then give me branch and total days, alphabetically. The register repeats some identical cards and has no home for a few slips; count matched loans once each.
objective: Deduplicate a lookup before joining, handle unmatched rows and aggregate values rather than counts.
hints: Two identical register cards should not turn one loan into two; a missing card cannot name a branch.
sort with distinct=True makes one lookup row per card, and group with sum adds days instead of counting rows.
Deduplicate by card and join; if no cards match, construct an empty table with the requested labels, otherwise select branch and days, group with sum, and rename the summed column.
inputCode:
import random
from datascience import Table, make_array
n = random.randint(3, 7)
keys = list(range(1, n + 1))
branches = [random.choice(['Fern', 'Reed', 'Willow']) for _ in keys]
copies = keys + random.sample(keys, random.randint(0, n))
register = Table().with_columns('card', make_array(*copies), 'branch', make_array(*[branches[key - 1] for key in copies]))
slips = [random.randint(1, n + 1) for _ in range(random.randint(4, 10))]
loans = Table().with_columns('card', make_array(*slips), 'days', make_array(*[random.randint(1, 15) for _ in slips]))
del n, keys, branches, copies, slips

fixtures.name: unregistered_slips
fixtures.predicate: any(card not in register.column('card') for card in loans.column('card'))

fixtures.name: empty_matching_cart
fixtures.predicate: all(card not in register.column('card') for card in loans.column('card'))

reference:
unique_cards = register.sort('card', distinct=True)
matched = loans.join('card', unique_cards)
if matched is None:
    deliver(Table().with_columns('branch', make_array(), 'total days', make_array()))
else:
    totals = matched.select('branch', 'days').group('branch', sum)
    deliver(totals.relabeled('days sum', 'total days').sort('branch'))

naive.code:
matched = loans.join('card', register).select('branch', 'days')
deliver(matched.group('branch', sum).relabeled('days sum', 'total days').sort('branch'))
